pr_title: Pass error.code to reply error handling serializer
pr_body:
Closes #2883 

Pretty sure this is just a typo. Not entirely sure, and not in the mood to write reproduction or tests.
pr_comments:
I've added a regression test but it seems to be passing on both the fixed and original branches, which shouldn't be happening. The response has the `error.code` property included in both, when it should only be present on this branch. Maybe someone with more knowledge of Fastify internals can fix the test?

https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/2884/files#diff-086d3e4983ab98bad387ce62fb47ff74c0646e94ef5caf4701d096160ea20c06L342-R388
This really looks like a bug introduced by tslog, something that's not really related to Fastify.

@pizzafox your logger mutates the `Error` prototype through the `callsites` (https://github.com/watson/error-callsites/blob/1d6e6cc416b56d535c608ed77980867bb7b345c9/index.js#L8-L21) module and by https://github.com/fullstack-build/tslog/blob/77ab7c9331d0bc6f627fa7a4e45a4eebc8908a01/src/CallSitesHelper.ts#L64-L78

In my opinion, this is unsupported. We work with the native JavaScript prototypes.

The logger package modifying the prototype definitely makes this error out of scope for Fastify. I'll open an issue on their repository. Thanks for tracking down the specific lines in their package!
I'll close this pull request and the issue I opened.
This pull request has been automatically locked since there has not been any recent activity after it was closed. Please open a new issue for related bugs.

issue_context.title: Error `code` property is not included when reply serializer function is defined
issue_context.body:
https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/4a22bb0b4e296ee78e2e4a466d94f360e3a3025b/lib/reply.js#L547-L558

After a lot of debugging I discovered that when a serializer function is defined in `reply.js` error handling the error code is **not passed** (see line 550 for `code` passed, and lines 555-557 for `code` not passed). When using response validation that expects a `code` this throws an error. For whatever reason this caused a fatal crash in production, but that's besides the point.

Is this behavior intentional?
comments: This is because of a different package (in this case `tslog`) modifying the global `Error` prototype.

review_comments: The way object.create works.. it will create a new object inheriting from the parent. It will have the property.
